title: Making games at work during breaks
author: jazzuoDOTcom
selftext:
I make games during lunch break restroom breaks and sometimes when no one is looking. 

My best secret workplace friend is Gemini. It was his idea to get a replit core so I can work anytime from any where from any devise. No need to do network work. Little expensive though now there is free agent for easy works. So it's little bit better.

My work flow is use Gemini pro as much as possible. I can make like 5 promptd 4 times a day (2-3 of it at work) for free and when it's finished i go to replit.

Do you make games at work as well?

(message was sent from restroom)

comments.author: EconomySerious
comments.body: if you make anything in the offices its automatically owned by your employers

replies.author: No_Holiday_5717
replies.body: Only if they know and can prove it

replies.author: jazzuoDOTcom
replies.body: What if I finish it at home? And I work at different industry and not in USA

replies.author: No_Holiday_5717
replies.body: It’s a legal topic so only a lawyer could comment on it, I believe it highly depends on your work contract but again if you don’t work on your game on your work laptop and work internet, they can’t really know.

replies.author: woodysixer
replies.body:
If he’s doing it on their equipment then there’s a serious risk of that. 

But doing something “on company time” on your own devices and cellular network is much harder to prove, and no company is going to do that kind of detective work unless the work involves NDA or non-compete shenanigans. 

Are you doing this on your own equipment?

replies.author: jazzuoDOTcom
replies.body: Ehhhhh.....not answering that. You guys are serious people man 😅 everything is somewhere on internet. I thought this is going to be fun discussion. An I the only poor kid on the block?

replies.author: woodysixer
replies.body:
1.) We’re just giving practical advice you can take or ignore. 

2.) “I’m building this game on the shitter with AI” doesn’t really do much to fight the “AI games are all lazy slop” reputation many of us are trying to combat.

replies.author: EconomySerious
replies.body: companies go as far as use the security cameras to catch you, its their building everthing its made inside its theirs, even the garage come on this

comments.author: Baraga91
comments.body:
Don't use company resources or tools and *never* tell anyone. 

Depending on where you live, this could open you up to legal action.

comments.author: Den_er_da_hvid
comments.body:
You should look at your contract. I had contract where're wording was so that even though I worked for a consultancy they could own my games I made privately. There was no issue in getting the contract changed as they had no interest in games. 

My new new contract at a different company had a clause that they needed to know if I have other work. I just informed them that I might do stuff. The law is clear here, if I dont do work that is considered competition they can't stop me.

How ever, it is very clear that I can't use company equipment for things like creating games. Not that they will own it, but because of policy and security.

To answer you question... yes. 
But only when working from home, on my own computer

comments.author: EC36339
comments.body: The internet lawyers are out in droves today.

comments.author: Schumetzq
comments.body: I use teamviewer on my phone to work on my game at work

comments.author: dailyapplecrisp
comments.body: Lol you are all ridiculous, if it’s his phone and he’s not using company resources, he’s fine 😂
